# Rig

> Rig is a free, open-source app (MIT licence) that tests whether a change to an AI coding agent really helps. It runs the same coding tasks with and without the change, each in its own Docker sandbox, and reports the difference with a 95% interval and a Rig score from 0 to 100. When the evidence is too thin to tell, it says so instead of guessing.

Rig runs locally: a Python engine serves a web app on 127.0.0.1, and nothing is hosted. It works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini, and runs for free on a local model (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM or Jan). Paid runs show an estimate first and stop at a budget you set.

What it can measure:

- A skill, a hook, an MCP server or a CLAUDE.md rule, with and without it on the same tasks.
- A change to the code itself, before and after, each side exported from git.
- A saving in tokens, cost or time per solved task, with the pass rate as a guard.
- A whole workflow, built on a canvas or started from one of 23 architectures, 15 business processes or 25 agentic patterns, on 20 built-in benches or an imported eval suite.
